title: Jitter damping for routing in long-span MoE experiments
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from experiments attempting to reduce p95/p99 jitter in MoE routing when serving very long contexts (>=64k tokens window equivalent) across Llama/Mistral/Qwen families. Goal: find lightweight runtime-level damping heuristics that reduce oscillatory routing behavior and PCIe/UVM stalls without heavy architectural changes.

High level hypothesis:
- Long-span requests increase router state churn (gating decisions + KV growth) and amplify tiny tokenization skew.
- This creates short-lived hot experts and backpressure on DMA + UVM when expert fanout spikes.
- Add a jitter-damping layer that (a) smooths routing probabilities over a tiny sliding window and (b) enforces a soft fanout cap to reduce instantaneous bursts. Expect lower tail latency and fewer page faults at slight cost to token throughput and potential small quality rejiggering.

Testbed:
- Models: Llama-70B-Long, Mistral-30B-Long, Qwen-14B-Long (weights quantized to int8 for a subset of runs)
- Hardware: 8x A100-80GB nodes; NVLink local staging for primary, fallback PCIe path active for cross-GPU traffic; UVM enabled in some configs to reproduce pagefault patterns.
- Workload: mixed-batch long-span traces (median 12k tokens, 90th 48k, heavy tail to 120k simulated with split windows). Tokenization skew introduced by synthetic prefix sets (wiki/news/codex style).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end request tail, GPU kernel stalls (ns), PCIe DMA queue depth, pagefault rate (/1000s), expert load imbalance (stddev per-step), throughput tokens/s.

Configurations tested:
1) baseline: current routing (hard top-2 gate, no damping), batching=auto, cache window=dynamic
2) soft-decay routing: per-token routing probs = alpha*prev + (1-alpha)*curr, alpha=0.6 over last 4 tokens
3) soft-cap fanout: allow top-k but with soft penalty after fanout>F (F=6) to probabilistically steer to next-best experts
4) both damping + soft-cap
5) adaptive prefetch window reduction: when pagefault rate > threshold, reduce prefetch window from 64 to 8 (eviction-friendly)

Key results (aggregated):
- Baseline p99 end-to-end: 1.49s per request under mixed tail (GPU-level p99 token latency 9.8ms)
- Soft-decay only: p99 reduced 27% -> 1.09s, token p99 7.2ms, GPU stall ns reduced 34%
- Soft-cap only: p99 reduced 18% -> 1.22s, expert stddev reduced 40% but throughput -6%
- Combined damping+cap: p99 reduced 41% -> 0.88s, token p99 5.7ms, pagefaults down 62%, throughput -9%
- Adaptive prefetch window triggered in 48% of long-tail requests and reduced pagefaults further but introduced transient latency spikes during window changes; best used with combined damping for stability.

Observed traces / root causes:
- Hotspot bursts: Many traces show a handful of adjacent tokens suddenly driving the same expert set due to tokenization boundary alignment. This causes instantaneous increase in memory reads/writes for KV and temporary fill of DMA queues.
- Oscillation: Router decisions flip across tokens for ambiguous inputs; without smoothing, this forces activation of different experts causing cross-GPU fetches and eviction churn.
- UVM thrash: When prefetch window was large, UVM page migrations combined with kernel scheduling led to 2–3x GPU stall durations during high-fanout bursts.
- Quantization sensitivity: Qwen int8 runs saw slightly larger sensitivity to damping (quality drop ~0.8 BLEU-equivalent on a held eval) vs float runs; Mistral had better resilience.

Profiling notes (commands & tools):
- Collected kernel traces via nvprof/nvtx and our internal token-trace plumbing: python tools/trace_runner.py --model qwen-14b-long --trace longspan-mix --nvtx
- DMA queue depth instrumented with perf counters and /sys GPU stats; cross-validated with nsys sampling
- Example flame slice: longspan_trace_0123: DMA enqueue latency spike aligned with router.forward at step ~413 leading to KV write stall of ~1.1ms.

Mitigations tried (and quick comments):
- Jitter-damping (soft decay): cheap, per-token state (4 floats per request); easy to turn on/off per-route; improves tail a lot for ambiguous gating workloads.
- Soft fanout cap: reduces instantaneous expert set size; needs calibration per model and impacts final quality slightly when cap low.
- Prefetch window adapt: reactive but oscillatory if threshold too aggressive. Combine with hysteresis.
- Ring-buffer micro-batching: queue small tokens into a tiny micro-batch window (max 2–3 tokens) to amortize DMA; reduced PCIe ops by 21% but adds p50 overhead ~4%.
- Locality-driven KV placement: try to prefer local experts when load comparable; requires routing-policy change at orchestration layer.

Quality impact / eval: 
- On a small eval set (prompt completion coherence + task accuracy), combined damping+cap had negligible degradation for Llama/Mistral (<0.3% metric diff) but Qwen int8 showed -0.8% on our code-completion metric. Decision: enable by default for non-quantized routes; gate-on for quantized after runbook confirmation.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Run extended 7-day canary with combined damping on a small percentage of hosted traffic; monitor quality regressions and pagefaults. (ENGINF-4321)
- Perf: add NVTX regions for routing soft-decay so we can quantify overhead in kernel timelines (PR #789 updates tracing hooks)
- Calibration job: autotune F (soft-cap fanout) per model family via historical traces (script: tools/fanout_autotune.py)
- Investigate deeper: could we avoid cross-GPU fetch by expert replication for top-2 hot experts? cost analysis needed.

Practical playbook (short):
1) Enable soft-decay alpha=0.6 on long-context routes (>=32k tokens) for 2 weeks in canary mode.
2) Add soft-cap F=6 only for Mistral and Llama on float routes; skip Qwen-int8 initially.
3) Keep prefetch window dynamic but add hysteresis: only shrink if pagefaults > 10/1000s for 30s sustained.
4) Monitor: p99 end-to-end, pagefault rate, expert stddev, token quality metrics.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a runtime-level mitigation so we can ship quickly; longer term we should look at gating model-quantization interplay and router-aware tokenizer smoothing upstream.
- Questions: what is acceptable throughput loss for Hosted tier? Should Dedicated customers get a toggle?

Slack threads / refs: #perf-longspan (internal), see thread pinned messages 2025-01-15 for initial traces.

Patch pointers: PR 789 contains a prototype short-lived soft-decay state and unit tests. The fanout soft-cap is behind a feature flag.

End of note.
